modelNotice: Longitudinal, linked-history, demographic and quantitative-clinical evidence model. Scores are relative pattern-consistency values, not diagnostic probabilities.

coverage.scope: Practical feline differential library with owner observations, longitudinal evidence summaries, structured clinical measurements, prior diagnoses, linked historical episodes, demographic context, and an explicit unmodeled reserve.
coverage.priorPolicy: Base hypothesis priors remain deliberately broad. Small source-backed demographic modifiers and explicit prior-diagnosis modifiers are applied transparently at inference time; these are heuristic context adjustments, not epidemiologic disease probabilities.
coverage.inferenceArchitecture: Raw observations are retained. Inference uses derived longitudinal summaries so repeated observations add persistence/recurrence information without being treated as independent duplicates.

urgencyRules.title: Breathing difficulty
urgencyRules.message: Labored breathing, open-mouth breathing, or blue-gray mucous membranes warrants immediate veterinary assessment.

urgencyRules.title: Unable to urinate
urgencyRules.message: Inability to pass urine is an emergency.

urgencyRules.title: Collapse or seizure
urgencyRules.message: Collapse, unresponsiveness, or seizure activity warrants emergency veterinary care.

urgencyRules.title: Sudden hind-limb paralysis / cold painful paws
urgencyRules.message: Sudden hind-limb paralysis or cold painful hind paws can represent a vascular emergency.

urgencyRules.title: Possible toxin exposure
urgencyRules.message: Known or suspected toxin exposure should be discussed with a veterinarian or animal poison service immediately.

urgencyRules.title: Possible gastrointestinal bleeding
urgencyRules.message: Blood in vomit or black/tarry stool can require urgent veterinary assessment.

urgencyRules.title: Straining to urinate
urgencyRules.message: Repeated urinary straining can progress to or represent obstruction and warrants prompt veterinary assessment.

urgencyRules.title: Jaundice observed
urgencyRules.message: Yellow discoloration of the gums, skin, or eyes warrants prompt veterinary assessment.

urgencyRules.title: Repeated vomiting with lethargy
urgencyRules.message: Repeated vomiting together with lethargy can indicate significant illness and warrants prompt veterinary assessment.

urgencyRules.title: Severe pain
urgencyRules.message: Severe or persistent pain warrants prompt veterinary assessment.

chronic_kidney_disease.note: CKD is highly prevalent in cats over 10.
Young age lowers, but does not eliminate, CKD consistency.

diabetes_mellitus.note: Male sex is a reported risk factor.
Increasing age is a reported risk factor.
Younger age modestly lowers consistency because risk increases with age.

hyperthyroidism.note: Hyperthyroidism occurs mainly in middle-aged to older cats.

feline_idiopathic_cystitis.note: Male cats may be at increased lower-urinary-tract risk.

urethral_obstruction.note: Male anatomy materially increases obstruction risk.
